## Projects Department Health & Safety Standards

Ref: EGY/PRJCTS/HSE/REQs

- The storage of materials and plantunderneath overhead power linesin prohibited
- >A method statement and permit to work is required for all work under overhead power lines.

## 3.9.Excavations

- >An excavation is any man made cavity or depression in the earth's surface, including its sides, walls or faces formed by earth removal and producing unsupported earth conditions (by reason of the excavation).
- Prior to excavation works a geotechnical survey is tobe carried out to determine soil characteristics, assess whether there is any contamination and enable the design (diaphragm walls, slope batters/benching etc.) to be determined
- Excavations are to be protected from collapsc by bcing bcnchcd, slopcd, shorcd (i.c. diaphragm walls, secant piling ctc.) as appropriatc. Slopes, benching and shoring are to be designed by a competent TemporaryWorks Designer.
- Drawings and the necessary licenses/permits are to be available on site and a permit to dig system shall be established and implemented prior to any cxcavation.
- A dewatering system is to be designed and installed at locations where excavations extend below type of work.
- The drawings and design showing the type of dewatering and groundwater control systems including proposals for discharge and the measures required to prevent damage surrounding infrastructure are tobe submitted toEMAARMisrforreview.
- Contractors arc to provide instruction and training to workers in safe digging techniques and a competent supervisor is tobe appointed to supervise all excavationworks.
- A Continuous solid barriers (minimum height of 950mm) or an earth safety bund is to be installed aroundallopenexcavationsexceeding1.2mindepth.
- Suitable access/egress (steps,ramps, secured ladders) is to be provided at regular intervals for all excavations.
- Excavated spoil formajorexcavationswill be immediatelyremoved from theworks area.Onsmaller excavationswhere spoil is tobekept close by it must beplaced a minimum of twometers clear of the edge of the excavation, this distance may need to increase depending on the overall depth and the methods adopted to prevent collapses.
- To prevent the risk associated with falling objects excavated materials, other materials and equiprment shall not be stored at the edge of any excavation. A clear distance of 2m shall be maintained around all excavations.
- Where there is a danger to the public,extra care shall be taken to properly cover all temporary openings and adequately barrier and sign the excavation. Flashing warning lights, signs and suitable lightingistobeinstalledwhererequired.
- Work shall not be carried out in an excavation unless the excavation and any work equipment and materials which affect its safety,have been inspected by a competent person:
